key_insight: A single deep learning model jointly predicts bioactivity and reconstructs molecular structures while providing a principled measure of distribution shift — enabling reliable exploration at the edge of chemical space and leading to discovery of active kinase inhibitors.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable generalization and hidden distribution shifts when applying molecular ML models to novel regions of chemical space, which hinders discovery of real bioactive compounds.
method: Train a multitask model that simultaneously performs molecular reconstruction (generative/autoencoding) and supervised bioactivity prediction to tie representation learning to prediction confidence.
Derive and use a principled metric for distribution shift/uncertainty from the joint model to identify out-of-distribution molecules and prioritize reliable predictions.
Experimentally validate the approach by screening predicted candidates and discovering active inhibitors for two clinically relevant kinase targets.
impact: Provides a practical recipe for safer, more trustworthy molecular ML: combining generative and predictive objectives improves representation robustness and gives actionable shift detection for deployment in drug discovery workflows.
